title: ML Engineer
description: Build and deploy machine learning models at scale. Design training pipelines, feature stores, and inference infrastructure.
starter_actions: Build 2 end-to-end ML projects with public datasets and documented eval metrics
Deploy at least one model as a REST API with monitoring and drift detection
Write about ML systems tradeoffs publicly — 2026 market rewards engineers who can explain decisions
Target companies with production ML teams: senior ML engineer median $193k, staff $240k+

title: AI/LLM Engineer
description: Build LLM-powered products — RAG pipelines, agents, evaluation frameworks, prompt systems. High demand, fast-moving field.
starter_actions: Build a RAG system with evaluation framework (not just vibes-testing) — 2026 hiring bars on eval skill
Open source one LLM agent with observable, measurable behavior
Specialize in agents or evals — AI Engineer median $206k, agents specialist $175k–$250k
Target AI-first companies and Series A–C startups; 58% of 2026 job listings require LLM/GenAI skills

title: Data Scientist
description: Analyse data, build predictive models, and communicate insights to business stakeholders.
starter_actions: Complete 2 Kaggle competitions and write up findings
Build a portfolio of business-framed analyses (not just notebooks)
Learn SQL deeply — window functions, CTEs
Target product analytics and growth roles as entry points

title: ML/AI Freelancer
description: Take contract projects building ML models, data pipelines, or LLM integrations for clients. Higher hourly rate, variable income.
starter_actions: Pick one niche (e.g. LLM integrations for SaaS tools)
Create a simple portfolio page with 2–3 case studies
List on Toptal, Upwork, or direct LinkedIn outreach
Price higher than you think — underpricing signals inexperience

title: AI Strategy Consultant
description: Help companies understand where AI applies to their business, evaluate vendors, and design implementation roadmaps. No code required — judgment and communication matter more.
starter_actions: Write 5 detailed posts on AI adoption mistakes companies make
Offer 2 free strategy sessions to build case studies
Target mid-market companies (50–500 employees) not enterprise
Package advice as audits: AI Readiness Audit ($2k–5k flat)

title: Technical Content Creator
description: Teach ML, AI, or data science through YouTube, newsletters, or courses. Monetise via sponsorships, courses, and affiliate income.
starter_actions: Pick ONE platform and ONE niche — do not spread thin
Publish 20 pieces of content before evaluating traction
Teach what you just learned — beginner's mind is an asset
Email list is the only asset you own — start it on day 1

title: ML/AI Course Creator
description: Build and sell online courses on ML, AI engineering, or data skills. One-time build, recurring revenue.
starter_actions: Validate with a free mini-course or cohort first
Sell before you build — pre-sell to 20 people at a discount
Host on Gumroad or Maven to avoid platform dependency
Niche down: 'ML for finance' beats 'learn ML'

title: AI SaaS Founder
description: Build a software product powered by AI/ML. Sell subscriptions. Full ownership, high risk, high reward.
starter_actions: Identify one painful workflow and automate it with AI
Ship an MVP in 2 weeks — not 2 months
Charge from day 1 — free users give bad signal
Talk to 10 potential customers before writing code

title: Data Engineer
description: Build pipelines, warehouses, and infrastructure that move and transform data at scale.
starter_actions: Build an end-to-end pipeline: ingest → transform → serve
Learn dbt and Airflow — they are everywhere
Get comfortable with a cloud data warehouse (BigQuery, Snowflake)
Data engineering skills transfer easily from DS/ML backgrounds

title: MLOps / Platform Engineer
description: Own the infrastructure that trains, evaluates, and serves ML models in production. High demand, smaller talent pool than DS/ML.
starter_actions: Deploy a model with FastAPI + Docker + CI/CD pipeline including automated eval gates
Add monitoring for data drift and model performance degradation — single most undervalued MLOps skill in 2026
Learn MLflow + observability stack (Prometheus/Grafana) — 63% of 2026 listings require MLOps tooling
Target companies with existing ML teams but no dedicated MLOps: highest leverage, fastest comp growth

title: AI Product Manager
description: Own the roadmap for AI-powered products. Bridge between technical ML teams and business/customers. Technical PM background valued highly.
starter_actions: Document your ML projects from a product impact lens
Learn product fundamentals: Jobs-to-be-done, PRDs, metrics
Target APM roles or internal transitions at tech companies
Your ML background is a strong differentiator — lead with it

title: ML Researcher
description: Push the state of the art in ML. Publish papers, develop new algorithms, work at research labs or academia.
starter_actions: Reproduce one recent NeurIPS/ICML paper fully
Write a clear explainer of a paper on LinkedIn or Arxiv
Apply to research internships or residencies (Google, Meta, DeepMind)
Strong math (linear algebra, probability, optimisation) is non-negotiable

title: AI-Augmented Writing Coach
description: Help founders, executives, and creators improve their writing using AI tools. Package as coaching, ghostwriting, or content strategy.
starter_actions: Build your own writing presence first — 50 posts minimum
Offer 3 free sessions, document results, build testimonials
Package as a 4-week sprint with deliverables
Target founders and technical people who hate writing

title: Dev Tools / OSS Builder
description: Build open source tools for developers or ML practitioners. Monetise via cloud hosting, premium features, or enterprise licensing.
starter_actions: Scratch your own itch — build the tool you wish existed
Ship early, get GitHub stars, iterate on feedback
Write excellent documentation — this is the product for dev tools
Monetise the hosted version (OSS core, paid cloud)

title: Prompt Engineer / LLM Specialist
description: Specialise in getting the best output from LLMs — evaluation, prompt design, fine-tuning strategy, and red-teaming.
starter_actions: Build a systematic prompt evaluation framework and publish it
Document 10 non-obvious prompting techniques with examples
Contribute to LLM benchmarking or evaluation repos on GitHub
This role evolves fast — follow the frontier weekly

title: Technical Recruiter (AI/ML niche)
description: Place AI/ML engineers at companies. Commission-based. Your technical credibility lets you qualify candidates and roles better than non-technical recruiters.
starter_actions: Build relationships with 20 AI engineers in your network
Partner with 3–5 early-stage startups actively hiring
Standard contingency fee: 15–25% of first-year salary
Your technical understanding is your entire edge here

title: Data Analyst
description: Answer business questions with data. SQL, dashboards, A/B test analysis. Lower barrier to entry than DS/ML, faster first job.
starter_actions: Build 3 portfolio analyses from public business datasets
Learn SQL deeply — this is the primary tool
Practice presenting findings, not just building dashboards
Good stepping stone to DS/ML roles with on-the-job data access

title: Early-Stage AI Startup (employee #1–10)
description: Join a pre-seed or seed stage AI startup as a founding engineer or early ML hire. Equity upside, fast learning, high uncertainty.
starter_actions: Target YC batch companies (current + recent batches)
Apply to roles directly via founder LinkedIn — skip job boards
Show evidence of shipping fast: side projects, OSS contributions
Negotiate equity seriously — it often exceeds salary value

title: Research Engineer
description: Implement and scale research ideas into production systems. Bridge between research and engineering. Found at AI labs (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind, etc.).
starter_actions: Reproduce a frontier model paper fully — document it publicly
Contribute to major ML OSS repos (Transformers, vLLM, etc.)
Strong systems skills (CUDA, distributed training) differentiate you
These roles are highly competitive — plan 6–12 months preparation

title: AI Implementation Agency
description: Build a small agency that implements AI solutions for businesses — chatbots, automation, analytics. Client services model.
starter_actions: Pick one vertical (legal, real estate, healthcare, e-commerce)
Build one reference implementation for that vertical
Price as projects ($5k–$50k) not hourly — better margins
First clients: warm network, local businesses, referrals

title: Backend Engineer (Java/JVM)
description: Build server-side systems in Java, Kotlin, or Scala. Enterprise-heavy stack — banking, e-commerce, logistics. Deep experience commands premium rates.
starter_actions: Build a REST API with Spring Boot, Postgres, and Docker
Learn system design — it dominates Java interview loops
Contribute to an OSS Java project to demonstrate initiative
Target fintech, e-commerce, and enterprise SaaS — biggest Java hirers

title: Backend Engineer (Python/Go)
description: Build APIs, microservices, and backend systems in Python or Go. High demand at startups and mid-size tech companies.
starter_actions: Build a production-grade API: auth, rate limiting, async tasks, tests
Contribute to a Python OSS project (FastAPI, SQLModel, etc.)
Deploy on Railway or Render first — cloud fundamentals matter
Python + Go combined is rare and very marketable

title: Backend Engineer (Node.js/TypeScript)
description: Build APIs and real-time systems in Node.js with TypeScript. Dominant at SaaS startups and frontend-heavy product teams.
starter_actions: Build a full-stack app: Next.js frontend + Node backend + Postgres
Master TypeScript — untyped Node.js is a red flag to senior engineers
Learn async patterns deeply: event loop, streams, worker threads
Target startups with React frontends — they almost always want Node

title: Frontend Engineer
description: Build user interfaces with React, Vue, or Angular. Own the browser experience — performance, accessibility, design systems.
starter_actions: Build 2 polished projects with React + TypeScript — design matters
Learn accessibility basics — it differentiates you from 80% of candidates
Master React internals: reconciliation, hooks, rendering patterns
Create a personal site that showcases work quality, not just lists projects

title: Full-Stack Engineer
description: Own the entire product surface — frontend UI and backend API. High leverage at startups where one engineer can ship a feature end to end.
starter_actions: Ship one complete product: auth, database, UI, deployment
Next.js + Postgres + Vercel/Railway is the fastest path to full-stack credibility
Target Series A–C startups: they need full-stack engineers most
Breadth is your pitch — show you can own a feature from design to prod

title: DevOps / Site Reliability Engineer
description: Own infrastructure reliability, CI/CD pipelines, and developer productivity. SRE roles at larger companies carry strong comp and high impact.
starter_actions: Get AWS Solutions Architect Associate certification — it's a baseline signal
Build a full CI/CD pipeline: code → test → build → deploy → monitor
Learn Kubernetes properly: deployments, services, ingress, resource limits
SRE roles need coding too — solid Python or Go scripting is expected

title: Cloud Architect
description: Design large-scale cloud infrastructure for cost, reliability, and security. Senior-level role — typically 7+ years experience, strong comp.
starter_actions: Earn AWS Solutions Architect Professional or Google Cloud Professional
Design and document a multi-region, fault-tolerant architecture end-to-end
Specialise in one vertical (fintech compliance, healthcare HIPAA, enterprise)
Architect roles rarely hire externally — build internally first, then move

title: iOS Mobile Engineer
description: Build native iOS applications in Swift. Consumer apps, fintech, health, and enterprise mobility are the biggest markets.
starter_actions: Publish one app to the App Store — the release process alone is a signal
Learn SwiftUI thoroughly — it is now the default UI framework
Study Human Interface Guidelines: Apple rejects apps that ignore them
Target companies with existing iOS apps over greenfield builds

title: Android Mobile Engineer
description: Build native Android applications in Kotlin. Larger global market share than iOS; strong demand in fintech, emerging markets, and enterprise.
starter_actions: Publish one app to Google Play — cover the full release cycle
Learn Jetpack Compose: XML layouts are becoming legacy
Build a multi-screen app with real data, offline support, and MVVM architecture
Android hiring is strong in fintech and logistics — target those sectors

title: Security Engineer
description: Protect systems from vulnerabilities, design secure architectures, run penetration tests, and respond to incidents. One of the highest comp-per-year-experience roles in tech.
starter_actions: Earn CompTIA Security+ then OSCP — the pair opens most doors
Practice on HackTheBox or TryHackMe before applying
Build a home lab: Kali Linux, vulnerable VMs, network monitoring
AppSec and cloud security pay more than traditional network security

title: QA / Test Automation Engineer
description: Own software quality through automated tests, CI integration, and performance testing. Underrated — companies that ship fast need serious QA.
starter_actions: Build a full automation suite for an open-source web app
Learn Playwright — it has largely replaced Selenium for web UI testing
Add performance testing (k6, Locust) to your skillset — high demand
Move toward SDET (Software Dev in Test) for better comp and scope

title: Database Engineer / DBA
description: Design, optimise, and operate databases at scale. Query tuning, schema design, replication, and disaster recovery. Critical at data-heavy companies.
starter_actions: Master query optimization: EXPLAIN ANALYZE, index strategies, partitioning
Set up a Postgres HA cluster with streaming replication from scratch
Learn one NoSQL store deeply (Mongo or Redis) — most stacks use both
Database skills age well — not subject to framework churn

title: Technical Writer / Documentation Engineer
description: Write and maintain developer documentation, API references, tutorials, and internal runbooks. High-value role at developer-tools companies.
starter_actions: Contribute docs improvements to one OSS project — merge is the portfolio
Pick a poorly documented API, rewrite its getting-started guide, publish it
Learn docs-as-code: Git, Markdown, static site generators (Docusaurus, MkDocs)
Target developer-tools companies — Stripe, Twilio, Vercel are benchmarks

title: Business Analyst / Systems Analyst
description: Bridge business requirements and technical implementation. Define specs, map processes, and validate that software solves the right problems.
starter_actions: Document a complex business process end-to-end using BPMN
Learn SQL to query data yourself — reduces dependency on engineers
Earn CBAP or PMI-PBA if targeting enterprise clients
BA roles are an underrated entry point for product management transitions

title: Product Manager
description: Define what to build and why. Own the product roadmap, user research, and success metrics. One of the highest-leverage individual contributor roles in tech.
starter_actions: Write 3 product teardowns of apps you use — publish them
Complete one product design challenge from a public case bank
Learn SQL to pull your own data — it removes the biggest PM bottleneck
Internal transfer is often faster than external hiring for PM roles

title: Solutions Engineer / Sales Engineer
description: Own the technical side of sales: demos, integrations, proofs of concept, and customer onboarding. Combine engineering depth with commercial awareness.
starter_actions: Practice giving live product demos — record and review yourself
Learn the full sales cycle: discovery, demo, POC, negotiation, close
Target B2B SaaS — SE roles are almost exclusively enterprise software
High OTE with commission: negotiate base + variable carefully

title: Scrum Master / Agile Coach
description: Facilitate agile delivery, remove impediments, and coach engineering teams on process. More valuable at scale than at startups.
starter_actions: Get Certified ScrumMaster (CSM) or PSM I — table stakes for the role
Volunteer to run a sprint retrospective at your current team
Learn SAFe if targeting large enterprise — it dominates that market
Agile coaching pays more than Scrum Master — build toward it

title: Fintech / Payments Engineer
description: Build financial infrastructure — payments, ledgers, compliance systems, and trading platforms. High stakes, high comp, strong demand.
starter_actions: Learn double-entry bookkeeping — it underpins every financial system
Build a simple payments API with Stripe — understand webhooks, idempotency, retries
Study PCI-DSS basics — knowing compliance requirements is a differentiator
Fintech companies pay 10–20% above market for engineers who understand money

title: Healthcare Tech / Digital Health Engineer
description: Build clinical software, patient data systems, and health AI applications. HIPAA compliance and interoperability (FHIR/HL7) expertise commands premium.
starter_actions: Learn FHIR R4 standard — it is the interoperability baseline across US healthcare
Understand HIPAA minimum necessary, BAAs, and audit logging requirements
Build a FHIR server integration as a portfolio project
Target telehealth, clinical decision support, and remote monitoring companies

title: Legal Tech Engineer
description: Build software for law firms and legal departments — contract analysis, e-discovery, compliance automation. Niche but growing fast with LLMs.
starter_actions: Build a contract clause extractor using an LLM + structured output
Learn the basics of legal document structure: contracts, NDAs, MSAs
Target LegalZoom, Clio, Thomson Reuters, or VC-backed legal AI startups
Legal AI is still underbuilt — domain knowledge + engineering is rare and valuable

title: Supply Chain / Logistics Tech Engineer
description: Build systems for inventory, demand forecasting, route optimisation, and warehouse management. Less glamorous than consumer tech; significantly more defensible.
starter_actions: Build a simple demand forecasting model on public retail data
Learn the basics of ERP systems (SAP, Oracle) — enterprise logistics runs on them
Study vehicle routing problems (VRP) and linear programming basics
Amazon, DHL, Flexport, and retail giants are constant hiring supply chain engineers

title: Backend Freelancer / Contract Engineer
description: Take contract work building APIs, services, and integrations for startups and SMBs. Higher rate than full-time, but you manage your own pipeline.
starter_actions: Niche immediately: 'Python backend' is too broad; 'FastAPI + Postgres for SaaS startups' gets replies
Create case studies for 2–3 past projects framed as business outcomes
Set a weekly floor: 10 outreach messages minimum until pipeline is full
Charge a project minimum ($3k–5k) to filter time-wasters

title: Frontend Freelancer / UI Developer
description: Build UIs and frontend features for clients on a contract basis. React dominates; Tailwind and Next.js are increasingly expected.
starter_actions: Build 3 polished UI projects with live demos — design quality matters
Offer a 'Design to Code' service: take Figma mockups and implement them exactly
List on Contra, Toptal, or Crew — frontend freelancers get hired faster than backend
Add motion design (Framer Motion) to your stack — it triples your rate ceiling

title: DevOps / Cloud Freelancer
description: Help companies set up infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, cloud migrations, and Kubernetes clusters on a contract basis. High-value, recurring engagements.
starter_actions: Package as a fixed-scope offering: 'AWS production setup' or 'K8s migration'
Get AWS Solutions Architect certified — clients use it as a trust signal
Cloud cost audits are quick wins: find savings, charge 10% of first year savings
DevOps freelancers are rare relative to demand — charge accordingly

title: Independent Software Consultant
description: Advise companies on technical architecture, team structure, technology choices, and delivery process. Senior ICs and ex-CTO types. No code required — judgment is the product.
starter_actions: Define one specific engagement type: tech debt audit, architecture review, CTO-for-hire
Write 5 posts on engineering decisions — this is your consulting signal
First clients come from past colleagues and warm referrals — start there
Retainer model beats project billing: pitch a monthly advisory engagement

title: HR Tech / People Ops Specialist
description: Implement, configure, and optimise HRIS platforms (Workday, Rippling, BambooHR). Intersection of HR domain knowledge and technical configuration skill.
starter_actions: Get Workday HCM or Rippling certified — vendor certs open doors fast
Learn to query HRIS APIs — most HR teams have zero technical depth
Target hyper-growth startups: they are overwhelmed with people-ops tooling
People analytics (Visier, ChartHop) is the premium tier — build toward it

title: Technical Recruiter
description: Source and place software engineers. Commission-based. Technical background — even adjacent — gives you a significant edge over non-technical recruiters.
starter_actions: Join an established agency first — solo recruiting without a track record is hard
Build a candidate pipeline in one niche before going broad
Standard contingency fee: 15–20% first-year salary
Technical credibility means you can have real conversations with engineers — use it

title: Software SaaS Founder (non-AI)
description: Build a vertical SaaS product for a specific industry or workflow. Slower growth than AI tools but more defensible with deep domain fit.
starter_actions: Start with a problem you have personally — founder-market fit matters
Talk to 20 potential customers before writing one line of code
Smallest possible scope: if it doesn't sell with 3 features, more won't help
B2B SaaS: charge more than you think, invoice annually, never go freemium first

title: Software Engineering Course Creator
description: Teach system design, backend, frontend, or DevOps through video courses, newsletters, or bootcamps. Passive income at scale.
starter_actions: Pick ONE topic: system design interviews, FastAPI, React — not all of them
Launch with a paid cohort before recording async video
YouTube short-form builds audience fastest — 1 video per week minimum
Gumroad or Lemon Squeezy for selling: avoid Udemy's race to the bottom
